This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the BMTC challenging by the judgment dated 21.02.2018 passed by MACT,
Bengaluru in MVC No.7005/2016.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 11.08.2016 when the claimant was walking on the left side of road, near Avalahalli Lake, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, at that time, BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-0567 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.

As a result of the aforesaid accident,
the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.687,855/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the BMTC to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

The learned counsel for the BMTC has raised the following contentions:

sentences.text: The accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the claimant himself.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the bus alone is negligent in causing the accident.
The accident occurred on 11.08.2016 and complaint has been lodged after two days from the date of accident and hence, there is delay in lodging the complaint.
In order to make a false claim, the claimant has lodged complaint against the driver of the bus.

The Tribunal has failed to consider the spot sketch and mahazar and only on the basis of FIR, complaint and charge sheet, the Tribunal has held that the driver of the bus is negligent in causing the accident.
QAUNTUM OF COMPENSATION a)

Firstly, PW-2, the doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered disability of 36%
to lower limb.
If one-third of the said disability is taken, it comes to 12% disability to NC: 2024:KHC:37143 whole body.
But the Tribunal has taken 18% disability to whole body, which is on the higher side.
b) Thirdly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, medical records and considering the age and avocation of the claimant, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.
7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following counter-contentions:
NEGLIGENCE
Immediately after the accident, the claimant was shifted to the hospital and he was not in a position to lodge a complaint.
Even the family members were busy in shifting the claimant from Sagar Hospital to SDM Hospital, Dharwad for providing treatment to the claimant.
Hence, there is delay in lodging the complaint.
The complainant, Muniraju, is the eye witness to the accident, as he was one NC: 2024:KHC:37143 of the passengers travelling in the offending bus.
Considering the materials available on record, the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.
QAUNTUM OF COMPENSATION
The claimant asserts that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
The doctor has stated that the claimant suffered 36% disability to particular limb.
Due to the accident, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
The case of the claimant is that on 11.08.2016 when the claimant was walking on the left side of road, near Avalahalli Lake, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, at that time, BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-0567 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sagar Hospital, Bengaluru and thereafter, he was shifted to SDM Hospital, Dharwad.

In Ex.P-11,
Discharge summary of Sagar Hospital, it is mentioned as "patients attendants wants to shift him to another facility at Hubli due to financial difficulties and others".
Therefore, it goes to show that the family members were busy and engaged in providing treatment to the claimant and busy in shifting him to SDM Hosptial, Dharwad.
Hence, there is delay in lodging the complaint.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Munirajy, who is the eye witness and one of the passengers in the offending bus, the police have registered NC: 2024:KHC:37143 FIR against the driver of the bus and after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus.
Therefore

, taking into consideration the evidence of the claimant, materials available on record such as complaint, FIR, charge sheet, spot sketch, spot mahazar and witness statement, this court is of the opinion that the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the bus alone is negligent in causing the accident.
Hence, the said finding of the Tribunal is confirmed.
QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION 10.
The claimant has sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and blunt injury to chest and abdomen with acute kidney injury.
The claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
The doctor has stated that the claimant suffered 36% disability to particular limb.
Considering the evidences of claimant and doctor, and medical records, this Court is of the opinion that the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal appears to be just and reasonable.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is dismissed.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The BMTC is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest as awarded by the Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
d) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursement.
